Nidus Prime

A relentless embodiment of the Infestation, Nidus Prime thrives in the chaos of the battle, growing stronger with every mutation. Harness his parasitic powers to ensnare enemies, unleash devastating attacks and bolster his own survivability. With no conventional shields to rely on, Nidus Prime is an excellent choice for Tenno who prefer an aggressive, ability-driven playstyle that rewards you the longer you stay in the fight.

Saryn Prime

A deadly plague given form, Saryn Prime spreads toxic devastation across the battlefield, leaving few enemies untouched. Infect foes with corrosive spores, empower your weapons with lethal toxins and unleash waves of viral destruction upon entire groups. Her exceptional area-of-effect damage makes her an excellent choice for Tenno who enjoy overwhelming enemies and clearing large crowds with ease.

items.title: Warframe’s Five-Year Plan
items.summary: What it takes to keep a live-service game from dying
items.content:
In early 2022, Rebecca Ford, formerly Warframe ’s director of community and live ops, took over as creative director, marking the beginning of a new era for the then-nearly-decade-old massively multiplayer space ninja fashion simulator. Taking the reins on such an established game would’ve been a daunting prospect for anyone, even someone as intimately familiar with it as Ford. But she and her cohort came armed with a plan.

The thing about game development, though, is that it’s fraught with unforeseen wobbles and stumbles, which can presage full-on faceplants. Even the best-laid plans rarely emerge from the process unaltered. Add to that the crucial fact that Warframe is a live-service game with its own daily, weekly, and monthly wants and needs; you can never entirely predict how its sometimes-obsessively dedicated player base will react to change.

So how can developers possibly lay down track to carry the game forward for five years while still leaving wiggle room to swerve? It’s an art, a science, and a math problem all rolled into one. Now, at the tail end of her first five years at the helm, Ford can reflect with clear eyes on what panned out, as well as what didn’t.

"You have to take big swings, or you join the statistic of the percent of live-service games that fail in a given year,” Ford told Aftermath. “One live-service game failing is a tragedy; one hundred a year is a statistic, and you must strive to radiate your DNA."

Warframe has long been prone to unexpected shifts in tone, subject matter, and even genre, with the past half-decade’s expansions taking players everywhere from a demented fantasyland , to the year 1999 , to World War 1-inspired trenches . But much of what’s happening in the game today—namely, a long-awaited journey to the star system that set the game’s whole story in motion, Tau —existed on a white board in Digital Extremes’ offices back in 2022.

During our interview, Ford walked me through it, pointing to recently revealed story beats like [SPOILERS] Lotus, the player character’s beloved space mom, cutting a deal with an Eldritch space horror known as The Man In The Wall to save all the child soldiers who pilot Warframes, as well as a more prominent role for Praghasa, Lotus’ mom who is also a spaceship [END SPOILERS].

“We really had the fundamental questions that felt relevant for Warframe —which [are] ‘What is The Man In The Wall? … Did Lotus cut a deal with The Man In The Wall? And then Praghasa, what’s going on with her?’—[mapped out],” said Ford. “Some of these will be very deeply explored in the quest that you're going to play at the end of the year with Tau. You can see the process from 2022 and us continuing to refine the timeline and what we think is important.”

By 2023, the team had already sketched out the intro to Tau , which finally debuted at this year’s TennoCon in London, Ontario and featured a noir detective-inspired Warframe, Brysko, skulking through the slums of a goopy, glistening city full of drug-addicted automatons.

“We knew [back in 2023] that Tau was going to be our addict arc, where it's like a Sentient-fentanyl parallel,” said Ford. “So all roads lead to Tau, and for three years we've been working in that direction, year over year.”

Another white board from 2023 featured a full chronological timeline of key moments throughout Warframe ’s centuries-spanning saga.

“For staging everything, white boards and analog are still so much how we work,” Ford said.

Ford also uses software to create a visual plan for every year, quarter by quarter, that outlines “all the big swings,” including the themes underpinning individual Warframes that will be released. This, however, is one place where Digital Extremes has decided to zig when it was planning to zag during Ford’s tenure as creative director.

Originally, a detective Waframe, Brysko, was going to be introduced in 2025, with his mini-story serving as the player’s first strides into Tau’s seedy underbelly. But then the team decided to move all of the Tau update to 2026, necessitating a new frame for that slot in 2025. Why? Because Warframe ’s ex-stewards, who’d since moved over to alpha-stage fantasy sister game Soulframe , had a great idea for an update that would serve as a lead-in to Tau : a leap back into the distant past known as The Old Peace . This would better establish the history between players’ faction, the Tenno, and the aforementioned Sentients, enemies turned allies (tragically) turned enemies again who are now the main occupants of Tau.

“We shipped a playable Old War,” said Ford, “which was a creative moment that the old team, Steve [Sinclair] and Geoff [Crookes], were like ‘You should really do this,’ and we were like, ‘Oh, you're so right. We'll add that to the plan to make Tau more impactful.’ So [ Tau and Brysko] got pushed back a year so we could make room for this.”

items.title: Warframe director promises new Tau expansion doesn’t mean the game’s original star system won't get new content
items.summary: Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford explains that the new Tau expansion doesn't mean the original Origin system will be abandoned.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Warframe director promises new Tau expansion doesn’t mean the game’s original star system won’t get new content Published:

Digital Extreme’s free-to-play behemoth Warframe is heading outside of its initial star system and into the Tau system. While brand-new adventures await, the studio is keen to note that they are not abandoning the system players have called home for more than ten years.

Since its 2012 PC alpha, Warframe has stayed mostly within the Origin star system. Outside of missions set in The Void, the PvE MMO has remained within one system, but with the upcoming Tau expansion later this year, players will be able to jump into a brand-new system.

Right now, players can already experience the prologue to this new expansion. Prologue to Tau, a new permanent quest, released earlier this month and is still ongoing, allowing fans to narratively prepare for the new expansion. But what comes after?

In an interview with Japanese outlet Denfaminicogamer , creative director Rebecca Ford explained that the future of Warframe is not entirely set in Tau. Instead, new content will come to both systems with no intention of leaving the old star system in the dust.

“Some might wonder if heading toward the Tau system means the Origin system will be left behind or forgotten,” Ford told the outlet. “But rest assured—whether you are a new player or someone returning to the game, there is no need to worry.”

Ford explained that the arrival of the Tau system only adds to Warframe’s universe with “new possibilities for the stories we can tell and the ideas we can explore”. While Warframe never felt restricted by its adherence to a single star system, the team believes exploring outwards invites new opportunities.

The creative director explained that the arrival of Tau will also mean more content in Origin. “It does not mean we are “finished” with the Origin system,” she said. “The Origin system remains a vital part of Warframe and will continue to be a significant focus in our future development.”

After a decade-plus of support, Ford is keen to note that Warframe is not slowing anytime soon. With the death of Destiny 2, Warframe has continued to grow , and Digital Extremes is keen to continue supporting the beloved online looter-shooter for years as it works on Soulframe, which will release eventually.

Lewis White is a veteran games journalist with over a decade in the field. Starting with beloved Xbox website ICXM/XboxMAD, Lewis became the Gaming Editor at MSPoweruser before becoming the Editor in Chief of StealthOptional and Gfinityesports. Lewis later jumped to By Gamers For Gamers where he jumped to become EIC of VideoGamer and the host of the New VideoGamer Podcast prior to the website’s acquisition.

Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

With a First Degree BA Hons in Games Journalism and Public Relations, Lewis has been a stable part of the British games press for over a decade, and has frequently displayed his love of Halo, The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and other games pretty much everywhere he’s worked. And FRVR is no different.

items.title: 5 Best Video Games Like Warframe
items.summary: If you dig the action in "Warframe" and are looking for something that will give you an analogous experience, check out these five games.
items.content:
Digital Extremes Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Warframe" is a video game that has stood the test of time for over a decade and continues to reward its loyal player base with fresh content, updates, and support. The game can't really be tethered to a single genre either, as it's an MMO, RPG, sci-fi-based story adventure, and looter shooter all wrapped up into a single package. While this makes the game feel accessible to a wide variety of players, it can also make it difficult for players to compare "Warframe" to any other game on offer.

Fortunately, some titles out there share one or more similarities with "Warframe" and can give you a comparable experience. While these titles might not be free-to-play and possess thousands of hours of content like "Warframe," they have at least one shared feature with the game that makes you feel like stepping into the suit of your Tenno all over again. Below, you'll find five games similar to "Warframe" and why fans might enjoy playing them.

Bungie "Destiny 2" is arguably the closest comparison to "Warframe" available in 2026. Both games are MMOs set in a sci-fi world with plenty of emphasis on developing the story. Not only that, but you'll also find that "Destiny 2" shares plenty of the same core elements as "Warframe," including collecting vast amounts of loot, selecting and customizing your character's class, and completing missions in co-op multiplayer. While it might sound like "Destiny 2" isn't anything different from "Warframe," that's not the case in the slightest, as the two play very differently, gameplay-wise.

"Destiny 2" is a fast-paced first-person shooter with a more challenging combat system that demands strategy and mastery over your weapons and skills. Raids present the most difficult challenge in the game, as these are large-scale events that reward a ton of loot, but there's plenty of individual content to take part in as well. Just like "Warframe," you can engage with this content as a solo player or in a party, and there are both PvE and PvP elements across a variety of modes and events. The two games might not play exactly the same, but "Destiny 2" is your best bet if you want something with all of the features that make "Warframe" great. However, it should be noted that developer Bungie has announced major changes to the future of "Destiny 2," which has caused a dip in player count.

Arrowhead Game Studios Compared to "Warframe," "Helldivers 2" offers a totally different experience from top to bottom. While both games have a sci-fi setting and feature co-op functionality, "Helldivers 2" doesn't really fall into any of the genres that define "Warframe." Instead, the game is a unique action-adventure experience that takes teamwork to a whole new level. "Helldivers 2" can't be played solo and requires four players to be in a party nearly at all times.

With your party, which can be comprised of friends or strangers that you match with, you'll drop into specific missions that are taking place all over a galaxy on different planets. You have various objectives you need to complete on these planets and a certain amount of time to extract before you fail the mission. When you're completing objectives, some of which are nearly impossible to finish , you can use a predefined loadout that you set before a drop starts. Your loadout can consist of weapons, gear, and special abilities that you unlock the further you progress. "Helldivers 2" is an entirely interactive and unique experience that doesn't offer the same narrative aspect as "Warframe," but its gameplay loop is highly rewarding.

NEXON "The First Descendant" is the only game on this list that primarily follows the "Warframe" model of being a free-to-play MMO looter shooter. While "The First Descendant" features far more monetization, the two games have a very similar gameplay style that "Warframe" fans will immediately recognize and be able to hop into. From the third-person perspective to the character customization to the overwhelming number of cosmetics, there's a lot to like if you're a "Warframe" fan.

Even the settings of the two games are similar, as "The First Descendant" takes place in a sci-fi universe where your character has enhanced abilities and travels to all sorts of different planets during the story. However, there's not a huge emphasis on the story, as "The First Descendant" is more about the loot grind than anything else. To obtain most rare pieces of gear, you need to research their designs, and you can do that by acquiring blueprints from various bosses and objectives. This can be a huge time commitment, though, as "The First Descendant" can have you repeating a boss for days before you get the drop you want.

Blizzard Entertainment From a strictly gameplay perspective, "Warframe" and "Diablo 4" are extremely different. One is a fast-paced third-person shooter MMO, while the other is a top-down ARPG with distinct character classes that alter your entire playstyle. However, if you take a look under the hood, "Diablo 4" has plenty to like if you're a "Warframe" fan.

For starters, "Diablo 4" places an enormous emphasis on loot, as every enemy and boss you kill has a chance to drop some rare piece of gear. While guns don't play a role in the loot, you can obtain weapons, such as staves or melee weapons, as well as jewelry and armor with certain traits that boost your character's abilities. "Diablo 4" also has an excellent base campaign filled with unique open-world zones, tough bosses, and progression. While you can also take on one of the several expansion campaigns, you can also engage in some PvP or the endgame grind that focuses on improving your loot and stats. Getting past the top-down view and alternate RPG mechanics might be hard at first for "Warframe" players, but "Diablo 4" is worth learning some new playstyles.

2K Arguably the most influential franchise in the entire looter shooter genre is "Borderlands," which helped define the genre back when the original game was released in 2009. While you could play any of the "Borderlands" games for a top-notch looter shooter experience, "Borderlands 4" is the most recent entry in the franchise. You don't need to play any of the previous games in the series to understand what's going on, either, so you can just hop right in.

Aside from the focus on looting, "Borderlands 4" and "Warframe" are both story-driven RPGs with open worlds and deep character progression. "Borderlands 4" can also be played with friends, as the series has been regarded as one of the best co-op experiences ever . However, there are more differences than similarities between the two games, as "Borderlands 4" is a first-person shooter with no PvP whatsoever. That said, the game is still an incredible experience, as you have a huge world to explore, vehicles to ride, and more loot than you'll ever know what to do with. It also features plenty of edgy dialogue and cutscenes, which often lead to some outrageous moments in both the main story and side quests. So, if you're looking for a witty and fun looter shooter RPG to hop into after a "Warframe" session, "Borderlands 4" certainly fits the bill.

items.content:
The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for your listening pleasure on major streaming platforms. "Devourer," was first heard during the Epoch Operation: Taubound Official Gameplay Teaser. Influenced by slow, heavy metal from the likes of Black Sabbath, it features lyrics "sung" in Voidtongue, the terrifyingly enigmatic language of the Untime. This was a deliberate choice, recalling the memorable moment from 2023's Whispers in the Walls Quest when you took control of one of Albrecht Entrati's Vessels for the first time. Here, these elements combine for a musical experience that feels as massive and imposing as your latest endeavors ahead of Warframe: Tau, coming later this year.

items.title: How to play the Prologue to Tau quest in Warframe
items.content:
How to play the Prologue to Tau quest in Warframe One of the late-game warriors.

Anyone can jump into the new Taubound event, but the Prologue to Tau mission is harder to access. This one is for the vets, and you'll need to have put in the hours if you want to experience it for yourself. The good news is that, unlike the event itself, this quest will stick around, so even if you cannot play it now, you will be able to once you get far enough into the game.

To play this quest, you need to have completed The Old Peace and The Hex story quests, the two most recent quests in the game. If you have done that, and go visit your Codex on your ship, you will be able to access the new Prologue Quest and Chapters section, Prologue to Tau.

I don't want to get into spoiler territory, but it's definitely a first for Warframe to have you do what you do in this quest. Once you wrap up the quest, you will be awarded the Taubound Honoria. After that, you can crack on with Epoch Operation: Taubound and start paving the way to the next chapter of Warframe.

items.title: Warframe Sets Course for a Distant Star System in Epoch Operation: Taubound
items.summary: In Epoch Operation: Taubound, new and returning XBOX players are invited to jump into missions on Eris in The Origin System, where they’ll destroy Infested enemies and obtain a new resource — Moonflesh.
items.content:
Community is the nexus of everything we do and every choice we make as Warframe developers. We create games with players, not just for players, and build trust over time through actions that demonstrate we listen. Our players around the world in our XBOX community are a monumental part of that family portrait; they help us make Warframe a better experience for everyone, and they deliver the critical feedback we need to ensure Warframe remains a safe, enjoyable space to spend a little time with friends and family online. To this day, I still pull out my XBOX 360 controller for our live TennoCon demos — it’s one of my favorite peripherals of all time.

Since Warframe debuted on XBOX One in 2014, we’ve thrived on stories and reports from our welcoming community of players across two generations of XBOX. In that time, we’ve brought them parity in content across platforms, introduced new ways to engage with a more global community with the introduction of cross-play and cross-save, and have dedicated platform-specific resources for players on XBOX to communicate with us directly.

From fan art, to handwritten thank-you letters, to bug reports and the constructive criticism we need to improve the experience day after day, and year after year, our XBOX community gives us the medicine we need to be stronger, smarter, and more inclusive. And we’re certainly not done yet.

From Warframe’s humble beginnings, we’ve teased the far-future narrative of Tau, a distant Star System shrouded in mystery. This year, we’re finally going together, and our community of XBOX players can help us get there. Alongside millions of players worldwide, we invite the community to join us in Epoch Operation: Taubound , arriving in Warframe on October 15. This unique, one-time community event will rally players everywhere, anywhere, for the ultimate cooperative challenge: fuel the trip to the distant Star System, Tau. Participation will be rewarded, and XBOX players won’t want to miss out before the event concludes on November 17.

In Epoch Operation: Taubound, new and returning XBOX players are invited to jump into missions on Eris in The Origin System, where they’ll destroy Infested enemies and obtain a new resource — Moonflesh — to power up the Sentient Mothership, Praghasa , and trade this curious new resource for event rewards. Coveted event rewards highlight what players on XBOX can discover and unlock alongside the community, including brand-new Armor Sets, exclusive event Honoria, Somachords, and other stunning cosmetics ranging from Glyphs, Sigils, Floofs, Syandanas, Signas, Badges, Blueprints, and so much more.

But that’s not all we have in store for our XBOX community. Also arriving is Prologue to Tau, a bite-sized entry in our single-player cinematic quest campaign that invites players to go hands-on with The Lotus for the first time ever (as seen during TennoLIVE 2026), setting the narrative stakes for this next monumental chapter in Warframe . Players can also finally use their Vessel they customized during TennoCon on the surface of Eris in a unique level and face off in a massive Infested boss fight. These permanent additions to Warframe ’s Quest Codex are not time-limited and are available to XBOX players who have completed The Hex and The Old Peace Quests.

From Tau and back, we are incredibly thankful to our XBOX community for being a part of this journey for 13+ years, and we look forward to the adventures ahead with you.

items.title: Korean-themed Warframe 'Narin' Wears a Gat and Dances with Ice Blades
items.summary: It has been a genuinely long time since I last launched 'Warframe'.I believe the last time I played intensely was before the pandemic, but due to the nature of my job, I couldn't stick with one game for long.
items.content:
Not an All-Rounder, but Excels in AoE Offensive Capability

Korean (한국어) KO Add us on It has been a genuinely long time since I last launched 'Warframe'.

I believe the last time I played intensely was before the pandemic, but due to the nature of my job, I couldn't stick with one game for long. Warframe is the kind of game that becomes more enjoyable the more time you invest in it. As much as I wanted to keep playing, playing various games is the destiny of a gaming journalist. Ultimately, despite having logged hundreds of hours into it, Warframe remained dormant in my library for quite a while.

Then, news of a new update arrived: 'Narin's Ice Blade'. While adding new Warframes is nothing unusual for the game, this Warframe was cut from a different cloth. An ability named Hakchum? A skin named Baridegi? What is this?

As you might notice, 'Narin' is the first Korean-themed Warframe. Given that Korea's image in the West is heavily tied to K-pop, I wondered if a Korean-themed frame would be music-focused like 'Octavia' or 'Temple'. Instead, we got a Cold-elemental Warframe wearing a gat and brandishing a rapier. Driven by curiosity alone, I had to try her out myself.

An Offensive Cold-Elemental Warframe Different from Frost

The quintessential Cold-themed frame in Warframe is undoubtedly 'Frost'. Released early in the game's service, Frost is tailored for defense, fulfilling the class fantasy of freezing and locking down enemies. However, 'Narin' takes a somewhat different approach. While Frost is a master of area control and denial, Narin dives into groups of enemies, instantly shutting down their movement, enduring incoming attacks, and wiping them out. Where Frost waits for enemies to approach, Narin takes the initiative and charges in.

Narin's ability kit is built around this exact concept.

Her first ability, 'Neote', lunges forward with her rapier and unleashes numerous ice orbs in front of her. While its raw damage isn't bad, the true value of this ability lies in rapidly stacking 'Ice' across multiple enemies rather than raw damage output. Since it has no particular cooldown, it's an ability you can freely spam whenever you see a crowd of enemies.

Her second ability, 'Naraemagi', absorbs Cold Status Effects from surrounding frozen enemies to restore Shields, granting Overguard if Shields are already at maximum. Since most of Narin's attacks freeze enemies solid, her survivability isn't bad to begin with, but Naraemagi provides a massive boost to her endurance. Even with minimal survivability modding, Naraemagi allows her to stay alive in most situations.

Her third ability, 'Hakchum', spreads ice wings upon cast and grants a floating effect. Players can adjust her altitude using the Spacebar and Control keys. Once positioned, clicking causes her to slam down, creating a wide Cold zone that applies not only Cold Status Effects but also a Cold Damage Vulnerability debuff. Hakchum boasts a fairly long duration, making it effective for defensive lockdown over an extended period. Because it continuously inflicts Cold status, it can also be paired with 'Naraemagi' as a panic button for survival.

Her ultimate ability, 'Nurinarim', is a visually stunning skill whose viability was revived through a recent hotfix. Once you fully fill your Ice meter using other abilities, Nurinarim becomes active. Upon activation, Narin performs an endless dance while a vast Cold area activates around her, dealing continuous damage to nearby foes. During this, she can launch powerful ice blade waves at enemies, which consume her Ice gauge by default—though the consumption rate is reduced based on enemy Cold Status stacks.

While the hotfix greatly enhanced Nurinarim's usability, its initial launch specifications were somewhat awkward, as blade waves could only be launched at enemies marked by Nurinarim. In most combat scenarios, when Narin activated her ultimate and began dealing AoE Cold damage, enemies instantly slowed down. Teammates never missed this window. Consequently, most enemies were wiped out before marks could even apply, making it difficult to execute the blade waves for heavy damage. Of course, the Cold Status Effect itself was still a huge asset to teamplay.

Her passive, 'Sangodae', is extraordinarily strong. Killing an enemy grants a 1% chance per Cold status stack on the target to drop a Sangodae pickup. Collecting it grants an additional 50% Cold damage to weapon attacks and abilities for 10 seconds. It's a straightforward, raw 50% damage boost with no catch.

items.summary: A new challenge arrives atop the Yuvan Peak, Tenno! Rally your squad, ring the Cryobell and overcome the Binds if you can. The Icebind is an experimental new game mode meant to give you the space to push your loadouts and tackle cooperative
items.content:
A new challenge arrives atop the Yuvan Peak, Tenno! Rally your squad, ring the Cryobell and overcome the Binds if you can. The Icebind is an experimental new game mode meant to give you the space to push your loadouts and tackle cooperative objectives. Six-player Squads. Level 999+ Enemies. Randomized modifiers known as Binds. Guaranteed Riven Splicer Rewards with bonus Rewards based on Side Objectives. Will you have what it takes to take on The Icebind? Learn more about The Icebind in our guide video below or in the full Dev Workshop.

To play The Icebind, you must have completed the Angels of the Zariman and Whispers in the Walls Quests as well as unlocked Elite Temporal or Deep Archimedea.

items.title: October in Warframe
items.summary: As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following e
items.content:
As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following events this month:

EPOCH OPERATION: TAUBOUND

October 15 - November 17 A unique event unlike anything you've experienced to date, Epoch Operation: Taubound offers all eligible Tenno the chance to become a part of Warframe history. If you want to help open up a path to the Tau System, be sure to have your account ready by completing the "Vor's Prize" Quest before October 15. Players looking to pilot their Vessel for the first time can also complete The Hex and The Old Peace in order to access a new, permanent Prologue Quest setting up the Road to Tau. For full event details – including prerequisites and more – click here.

NIGHTS OF NABERUS

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Spooky season returns to the Origin System during our annual Halloween-inspired event, with Daughter releasing her inventory of new and returning seasonal Customizations in exchange for Mother Tokens. While Baro Ki'Teer will mark the occasion in the same unsettling fashion as last year (IYKYK), we're also mixing it up by bringing back the Hallowed Nightmares Tactical Alert, allowing you to face off against the fearsome Jack O'Naut for even more Naberus treats. For all the harrowing details, check out our Halloween 2026 Events post.

NEW GAME MODE: THE ICEBIND

October 7 Originally intended to ship alongside Iceblade of Narin as "Glacial Defiance," our new 6-player game mode was ultimately delayed to allow for additional development time and renamed to The Icebind. Accessible in-game starting October 7, these challenging, high-level Missions can be played up to three times weekly, allowing you to put your teamwork (and Loadouts) to the test for valuable Rewards. Visit the official Warframe Forums to learn more about the delay, and further details of the game mode itself.

PRINCESS MARGARET CANCER FOUNDATION QUEST

October 1 - October 31 PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation light the way towards a world free from the fear of cancer. Visit the Warframe PMCF Quest webpage for more information or donate directly here.

items.title: Protea Prime and Ivara Prime Enter Prime Resurgence
items.summary: Protea Prime A master of battlefield preparation, Protea Prime brings tactical ingenuity and devastating technology to every mission. Deploy her arsenal, control the flow of combat and keep your squad supplied while turning the battlefield
items.content:
Protea Prime

A master of battlefield preparation, Protea Prime brings tactical ingenuity and devastating technology to every mission. Deploy her arsenal, control the flow of combat and keep your squad supplied while turning the battlefield to your advantage. Protea Prime is a versatile addition to any Arsenal, giving Tenno the tools to adapt to whatever the Origin System throws their way.

Ivara Prime

Stalking from the shadows and waiting for the perfect moment to strike, Ivara Prime is a huntress ready to claim her prey. Ivara Prime draws her bow and disappears into the shadows before striking with deadly precision. With a versatile Quiver, powerful Artemis Bow and the ability to move unseen, Ivara Prime is a natural choice for Tenno who prefer stealth and careful execution.

Prime Warframes

Want to learn more about Prime Warframes? Check out our Guide to Prime Warframes video for a helpful breakdown of what Prime Warframes are, different ways you can earn them and how you can purchase Prime items.

items.title: PMCF Quest 2026
items.summary: PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help us support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation
items.content:
PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help us support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation. There are multiple ways to show support and make donations!

Watch on Twitch

Watch official Warframe and participating Warframe Content Creator livestreams and donate via the Team Warframe Tiltify donation page.

Conquera Merch

Help us reach every donation goal while reinforcing your IRL Arsenal! Check out the all-new Conquera Merch available this year. Total net-proceeds from sales of Conquera Merch will be donated at the end of the campaign.

In-Game

Support alongside fellow Tenno by picking up squishable versions of Valkyr and Voruna from the in-game Market! Purchasing these Floofs with Paid Platinum will contribute to the collective goal of selling both 40,000 Voruna Floofs and 40,000 Valkyr Floofs! Digital Extremes will donate an additional $20,000 CAD towards the PMCFQ campaign once each of these goals have been met. They will also become available to purchase with Personal Platinum at the time that they reach their respective goal. See all the Rewards and the full livestream schedule including our epic finale at warframe.com/pmcfq

items.title: Warframe’s Halloween 2026 Events
items.summary: With Iceblade of Narin now live, there's lots to see and do at Yuvan Peak and elsewhere aboard the Zariman. But after you've had a chance to explore our latest update, the spooky season beckons… Move from the chilly to the chilling with a l
items.content:
With Iceblade of Narin now live, there's lots to see and do at Yuvan Peak and elsewhere aboard the Zariman. But after you've had a chance to explore our latest update, the spooky season beckons… Move from the chilly to the chilling with a look at Warframe's seasonal October content below:

Nights of Naberus

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Your favorite spine-tingling, seasonal event is back with a bevy of bone-chilling items available from Daughter in exchange for Mother Tokens. Alongside a full inventory of previous offerings, you'll also find some tempting new treats, including:
  • Calaverita Liset Skin
  • Follie Coulrophobia Glyph
  • Voruna Prime Massacre Glyph
  • Sirius vs. Orion Poster
As in years past, Mother Tokens can be obtained by completing Bounties in the Cambion Drift, or by trading additional Resources with Grandmother.

Hallowed Nightmares

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET During the Nights of the Naberus, you'll have the opportunity to take on a Halloween-themed Tactical Alert not seen for several years. Face down the fearsome Jack O'Naut to earn the all-new Jack O’Naut Keychain Sugatra along with:
  • Jack O'Naut Recall Glyph
  • Manic Noggle
  • 50,000 Credits

"Scare-o" Ki'Teer Returns

October 16 @ 9 a.m. ET - November 8 @ 9 a.m. ET The Void Trader's vexing variant will once again make a series of weekend appearances all month long, offering his usual wares along with some beautifully baleful items you haven't seen before! If you enjoyed his unique inventory last time around, you won't want to miss what he's bringing to this year's bizarre bazaar starting at 9 a.m. ET and ending at 9 a.m. ET on the following dates:
  • Visit 1: October 16 - October 18
  • Visit 2: October 23 - October 25
  • Visit 3: October 30 - November 1
  • Visit 4: November 6 - November 8

Tennotober

October 1 @ 12:01 a.m. ET - October 31 @ 11:59 p.m. ET It wouldn't be fall without Tennotober, Warframe's community art challenge supporting the Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation Quest. Find this year's guidelines and prompts on the official Warframe Forums, where you can share your illustrations and Capturas to participate.

Excalibur Nights of Naberus Plushie Giveaway

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - October 9 @ 11 a.m. ET We've collaborated with our friends at Makeship to bring you a delightfully devilish new plushie version of Excalibur. Adorned with the Nyctalus Ephemera and colored for the occasion, the master swordsman looks markedly malevolent yet cuddly as ever. We're giving one away to three lucky Tenno who enter our giveaway via Gleam.
